import pandas as pd
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
pd.DataFrame({'id':[1,2], 'val':[10,20]}).to_sql('t', conn, index=False)
df = pd.read_sql('SELECT * FROM t WHERE val > 15', conn)
print(df['id'].tolist())
questions.explanation: Only row with val=20 satisfies val>15, its id is 2.

questions.question: Given the SQL query below, what does it return (assume tables exist)?
questions.codeSnippet:
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.cust_id
GROUP BY c.name
HAVING order_count = 0;
questions.correctOutput: Names of customers with no orders
questions.correctAnswer: Names of customers with no orders
questions.explanation: The LEFT JOIN combined with HAVING COUNT(o.id)=0 finds customers without matching orders.
